pinterest.title: Travel Advisor Benefits for a Destination Wedding: What Is Harder to Arrange Alone
pinterest.description: A destination wedding is more than a flight: villas, a venue, a photographer, guests arriving from three cities and deposits due in two currencies. Travel advisor benefits sit there. A good advisor gives you one point of contact, quotes in Australian dollars, the fee agreed in writing before any work begins and every inclusion confirmed in writing before you pay. Read the full guide.

pinterest.title: Questions to Ask a Travel Advisor Before You Sign
pinterest.description: Before you agree, ask any travel advisor how their fee is charged and whether it is in writing, what each quote includes, what the cancellation and change terms are for the advisor and each provider, whether they hold insolvency insurance, and how overseas payments are made. Then arrange travel insurance early. Save this checklist and read the full guide.

pinterest.title: What You Can Book Yourself and Where a Travel Advisor Helps Most
pinterest.description: Many couples book their own flights and honeymoon stays, and do it well. It gets harder once the trip is a wedding: guests to track, several suppliers each with their own deposit date and terms, and payments in more than one currency. Your consumer guarantees are the same whether you book direct, through an agent or through a booking platform. See where you sit in the full guide.

instagram_carousel.caption:
You can book a flight in minutes. A destination wedding is something else: flights, villas, a venue, a photographer, guests arriving from three cities and deposits due in two currencies.

That is where travel advisor benefits sit. Each piece is possible on your own. Together, they are harder and slower to arrange alone. A good advisor makes these easier:
1. One point of contact from flights to the ceremony.
2. Quotes in Australian dollars, so you can compare options side by side.
3. Inclusions confirmed in writing before you commit.
4. Someone working in your time zone.
5. Venue, travel, vendors and payments planned together.
6. Both sets of terms, the agent's and each provider's, read before you pay.

What does not change? Your rights. The consumer guarantees are the same whether you book direct, through an agent or through a booking platform.

Plenty of couples book their own flights and honeymoon stays. It gets harder with guests to track, many suppliers and payments in several currencies.

Before you agree to work with any advisor, ask how the fee is charged and whether it is in writing, what each quote includes, what the cancellation terms are, whether they hold insolvency insurance, and how overseas payments are made. Then arrange travel insurance early.
